title: Kernel of the explicit Veronese fraction map
statement: For any scheme X [def-pc-scheme], invertible module L [def-sc-invertible-module], natural number d and s in degree d of its section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], let g be the explicit additive map of [def-sc-section-ring-veronese-fraction-map] and let R be the fraction-relation submodule of [def-sc-section-fraction-presentation] for M=L tensorPow d, F=O_X and sigma=s_d. Then R, regarded as an additive subgroup of the numerator direct sum, equals ker(g). This states equality of subgroups for a fixed constructed map, without a generator formula for any unspecified equivalence.

source.place: Equation module-invert-s (Tag 0B5L), Lemma 01PW(2), and the Veronese localization in the proof of Lemma 01Q1

proof.text: Write T_n for the explicit numerator isomorphism of [def-sc-section-ring-veronese-fraction-map]. On each open set trivializing L, both the section-ring product and tensor-power transition multiply coefficient functions in the structure sheaf; the tensor-power isomorphisms preserve powers of the chosen generator. Glue to obtain a_(n+b)(transition_n,b(t))=a_n(t)*s^b, where a_n(t)=of_(nd)(T_n inverse(t)). The same local calculation identifies global-function scalar multiplication with multiplication by the degree-zero ring element. Every transition difference and every scalar multiple maps to zero; additivity kills their whole submodule span.

For a finite-support numerator family z in the kernel, choose N at least every support index. Subtract the transition difference from each index n to N, so z is congruent modulo the relation submodule to a single generator of degree N with numerator t. Its image a_N(t)/s^N is zero. The localization equality criterion gives k>=0 such that s^k*a_N(t)=0. The coherence identity and injectivity of the degree-(N+k)d injection and numerator isomorphism show that transition_N,k(t)=0. The degree N to N+k relation then puts the single generator, hence z, in the relation submodule. Empty support, d=0 and nilpotent s require no changes. This proves the reverse kernel inclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem sectionRingVeroneseFractionMap_kernel
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (d : ℕ) (s : sectionRingGrade L d) :
    (sectionFractionRelations (L.tensorPow d) (𝟙_ X.Modules) (s.val d)).toAddSubgroup =
      (sectionRingVeroneseFractionMap X L d s).ker
